stem: A 13-year-old boy with a high BMI attends for pubertal assessment and his mother is worried that his penis looks very small, but the shaft appears hidden within surrounding tissue; what is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Buried penis in a boy with high BMI
Retractile testes due to a hyperactive cremasteric reflex
Arrested testicular descent from the kidney

explanation: Buried penis in a boy with high BMI is the most likely explanation. In boys with high BMI, surrounding suprapubic tissue can conceal the penile shaft and make the penis appear smaller than it is.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because increased suprapubic tissue in a boy with high BMI can conceal the shaft and create the appearance of a small penis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because intravaginal torsion is a form of testicular torsion, not a cause of a hidden penile shaft.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because bell-clapper malformation predisposes to testicular torsion, not penile concealment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because retractile testes involve testicular position, not the appearance of the penis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because arrested testicular descent refers to cryptorchidism, which is unrelated to a buried penile shaft.
